## The specification menu {#the-specification-menu .smaller}

```{r}
#| label: menu-table
#| output: asis
# The eleven decisions of the menu (data/menu_options.csv), with the options
# that the curve keeps and the others grouped by the workshop's judgement.
judgement_txt <- c(other_question = "another question", weaker_answer = "a weaker answer",
                   check = "a check", unavailable = "not in the public file")
level_txt <- c(estimand = "Question", measurement = "Measurement", estimation = "Model")
off_txt <- menu_opts |>
  dplyr::filter(!on_curve) |>
  dplyr::summarise(txt = paste0(paste(label, collapse = ", "), " *(", judgement_txt[dplyr::first(judgement)], ")*"),
            .by = c(axis, judgement)) |>
  dplyr::summarise(off = paste(txt, collapse = "; "), .by = axis)
menu_rows <- menu_opts |>
  dplyr::filter(on_curve) |>
  dplyr::summarise(level = dplyr::first(level), decision = dplyr::first(decision),
            on = paste(label, collapse = "; "), .by = axis) |>
  dplyr::left_join(off_txt, by = "axis") |>
  dplyr::mutate(off = dplyr::coalesce(off, "–"),
         level = dplyr::if_else(level == dplyr::lag(level, default = ""), "", level_txt[level]),
         line = paste0("| ", level, " | **", decision, "** | ", on, " | ", off, " |"))
cat(c("::: {.fs-55}",
      "| Group | Decision | On the curve | Off the curve |",
      "|:--|:--|:--|:--|",
      menu_rows$line, ":::"), sep = "\n")
```

::: {.small}
Five decisions keep more than one option, and they cross into the **`r nrow(curve)`** specifications of the curve. The [decision map](../menu.html#map) gives the reason for every option.
:::

::: notes
This is the menu on which the rest of the part is built, the full list of the decisions that any analyst of this claim has to take, eleven of them in three groups. The decisions about the question settle what is asked: the outcome, the comparison group, which emails are counted, which names and whose replies. The decisions about measurement settle how the outcome is counted, for the five replies whose greeting nobody coded and for the emails that bounced. The decisions about the model settle how the answer is reached, through the model, the covariates, the test and the scale of the result. Every option on the right was considered and left off the curve for a stated reason, because it answers another question, answers this one less well, serves as a check, or cannot be fitted on the public file, and the decision map on the workshop's website gives the reason for each.
:::

## The curve of 64 {#the-curve-of-64 .smaller}

::: {.small}
- **Comparison group** – white names, or white and Black names
- **Emails counted** – replies only, or all delivered emails
- **Replies without a greeting code** – left out, or counted as no greeting
- **Model form** – a difference in proportions, or logistic regression
- **Adjustment** – none; hard-to-find address; place, without ethnic composition; or place, with ethnic composition
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 4 = **`r nrow(curve)`**. The reference specification is the raw gap of the paper: `r fmt_num(curve_ref$rate_hisp, 1)`% against `r fmt_num(curve_ref$rate_comp, 1)`%, **`r fmt_num(curve_ref$b_pp, 2)` points**, *t* = `r fmt_num(curve_ref$stat, 2)` on `r curve_ref$df` df, n = `r curve_ref$n` replies.

```{.r}
try_spec(comparison = "white", population = "replies", uncoded = "drop",
         model = "lpm", adjust = "none")
```
:::

::: notes
Five of the eleven decisions keep more than one option on the curve: the comparison, with the white names or with the white and Black names; the emails counted, the replies or every delivered email; the five uncoded replies, left out or counted as replies without a greeting; the model, a difference in proportions or a logistic regression; and the adjustment, four sets of covariates from none to the set of the original model, in the thirds of the public file. [advance] Two times two times two times two times four gives sixty-four specifications, and every one has been fitted. The reference specification is the raw gap of the paper, the Hispanic against the white names among the replies with no covariates, forty-one against sixty-one per cent, a gap of twenty points. Every argument of try underscore spec defaults to that reference, so a change of one decision is a change of one argument.
:::

## Ground rules for the menu {#one-deviation-and-a-reason-for-it .smaller}

::: {.small}
- **Change one decision at a time**, and hold the others at the reference specification. When a result moves, you can then say what moved it
- **An option off the curve is refused** by `try_spec()`, with the reason from the menu and the page that teaches it. Asking for one is part of the exercise
- **One sign convention:** every estimate is Hispanic minus comparison names, in percentage points, so below zero is the direction of the claim
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
The estimand statement on the [decision map](../menu.html#map) rewrites itself as you choose. A change in its first sentence asks another question, a change inside its parentheses counts the outcome differently, and a change in the second sentence reaches the answer another way.
:::

::: notes
Three ground rules before you touch the menu. First, change one decision at a time and hold the others at the reference, which keeps the class chart readable, because when a result sits somewhere surprising we can say what put it there. Second, if you ask for an option that is off the curve, try underscore spec refuses it, says why and names the page that teaches it, and asking for one is part of the exercise, since the reason for the refusal is what you are meant to read. Third, one sign convention binds everybody: every estimate is the Hispanic names minus the comparison names, in percentage points, so that below zero is the direction of the claim. [advance] The decision map on the workshop's website rewrites the estimand statement as you choose, and so shows whether a choice changes the question or only the way of answering it.
:::
